item.title: Open Innovation in Action: People, Processes and Performance of R&D Management
item.content:encoded:
This Special Issue is part of a coordinated set of activities, including a Festschrift Conference in Rome (April 20-21, 2026) and complementary Special Issues in R&D Management, Industrial and Corporate Change (ICC) and California Management Review (CMR), to celebrate Professor Henry Chesbrough's seminal contributions to the field of Open Innovation (OI).

Potential topics

  • Open Innovation
  • R&D Management
  • People in R&D
  • Processes in R&D
  • Performance of R&D

Timeline

  • September 15, 2026: Deadline for Submissions

item.title: Back to basics in R&D Management: Rediscovering the importance of company case studies
item.content:encoded:
This special issue aims to reverse the trend of declining case study research, rediscovering and reaffirming the value of case studies on the organization and management of R&D to capture the nuances of this specific function in organizational settings and to provide actionable insights for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers. By bringing practical perspectives back to the forefront with a focus on single and multiple case studies, the special issue aims to reconnect theoretical developments with the direct experiences of companies managing innovation on the ground.

Potential topics

  • Case studies on the organization and management of R&D
  • Single and multiple case studies of R&D management
  • Practical perspectives on managing innovation in organizational settings
  • Reconnecting theory with company experiences in R&D management
  • Nuances of R&D function in organizational contexts

Timeline

  • November 1, 2026: Submission window opens
  • December 31, 2026: Submission window closes

item.title: Capturing Value in the Digital Era: Organizing for Innovation Protection and Information Security
item.content:encoded:
R&D Management has a rich publication history in research on appropriability, intellectual capital and capturing value from innovation. This special issue seeks to update and extend that tradition by explicitly bringing together two adjacent but typically separated conversations.

The first conversation conceptualizes protection of innovation in relation to appropriability mechanisms such as patents, trade secrecy, licensing, contracting, complementary assets, and ecosystem governance to investigate value capture potential.

The second conversation - so far mainly happening in information systems and engineering journals - conceptualizes protection of innovation as information security, such as the protection of R&D artifacts, risks of leakage and theft, industrial espionage, and applications of organizational secrecy for R&D purposes.

Potential topics

  • Appropriability mechanisms such as patents, trade secrecy, licensing, contracting, complementary assets, and ecosystem governance
  • Value capture potential from innovation
  • Protection of R&D artifacts
  • Risks of leakage and theft in innovation
  • Industrial espionage
  • Organizational secrecy for R&D purposes
  • Information security in innovation management
  • Intellectual capital and capturing value from innovation

Timeline

  • February 1, 2027: Submissions open
  • April 30, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: The Non-Human Innovator: Agentic AI, Physical AI, and the Transformation of R&D Management
item.content:encoded:
This Special Issue is explicitly positioned around a question that existing work on AI-enabled knowledge search, collaboration management, and general AI governance has not yet answered: what happens when AI ceases to be a mere instrument and becomes an agent of innovation? This distinction — between AI-as-tool and AI-as-innovator — defines the conceptual boundary of our four research themes, which address the optimal human–AI division of innovative labour, the architecture of autonomously populated innovation ecosystems, the reimagination of absorptive capacity for an agentic era, and the fundamental challenges to IP posed by non-human inventorship.

Potential topics

  • Optimal human-AI division of innovative labour
  • Architecture of autonomously populated innovation ecosystems
  • Reimagination of absorptive capacity for an agentic era
  • Fundamental challenges to intellectual property posed by non-human inventorship

Timeline

  • June 30, 2027: Deadline for submissions
